title: Oxidase Test
principle: Detects the presence of cytochrome c oxidase, an enzyme in the electron transport chain of some aerobic and facultatively anaerobic bacteria. The reagent (a redox dye, commonly tetramethyl-p-phenylenediamine) is oxidized by the enzyme, producing a dark purple/blue color change.
purpose: Used to help distinguish oxidase-positive genera (e.g. Pseudomonas, Neisseria, Vibrio) from oxidase-negative Enterobacteriaceae, as part of a broader identification scheme.
reagents: Oxidase reagent (e.g. 1% tetramethyl-p-phenylenediamine dihydrochloride), typically on a filter paper strip or disk

procedure.instruction: Using a sterile plastic loop or wooden applicator stick (not a nichrome/iron loop, which can give a false positive), rub a small amount of colony growth onto the oxidase reagent strip/disk.
Observe the color change over the timeframe specified by the specific reagent product being used.

positiveResult: Development of a dark purple/blue color, typically within the timeframe stated on the specific reagent product's instructions.
negativeResult: No color change within that timeframe.
interpretation: A positive result indicates cytochrome c oxidase activity; timing matters, since a color change appearing well after the product-specified window is not considered a true positive by most protocols.
precautions: Never use a nichrome or iron-containing loop — metal ions can produce a false-positive reaction with the reagent.
Read within the product-specified timeframe; late color changes are not reliable indicators.
limitations: Reagent strips degrade with light/air exposure over time and can give unreliable results if expired or improperly stored.
